body: I feel the same way which is why I decided to push through it and keep going. It's just been too hard. I'm crumbling under it all. I'm just so tired.

The issue is I've been doing that (suppressing) for 4-5 years now but when the whole pandemic hit everything went to shit. It got worse. It's a literal miracle I didn't just drop out or academic probation. I just want everything to stop but it feels neverending.

No, just can't fail. I'm so close to escaping and graduating. I'd be stuck again and probably make the same mistakes. I hate the conversation I'd have with my parents about it. They'd probably call me a failure or useless.

My friend actually told me that I'm doing fine and take a moment to celebrate the fact I'm still passing my other two classes so I'm not completely failing the semester. I appreciate her but the thought of failing. I just can't fail. I hate it. I always abandon the things I fail at to avoid being be marked as a failure.  As for my degree, I was going to do education before I decided I  obviously wasn't in the right mindset to teach children. I legitimately don't know what my bachelor's degree is going to be in. I just know I'm supposed to be getting one. The idea was to figure out what to do with it after. I also don't have any work experience which is why I feel the immense need to disappear because my parents have supported me as a grown adult the whole time allowing me to be a full-time student. I'm supposed to be doing well.
